about: What a Ruby (Googlebook) image may run that reaches PC firmware, the TPM or the embedded controller. scripts/googlebook/check-firmware-safety.py applies it to partition trees, images and payloads; the on-laptop adapter (ANAL-229 phase 3) applies the same file. Any unreviewed match fails closed. Patterns are RE2-compatible (Go) and Python re.
rc_scope: Every *.rc file in every partition and APEX, comment lines (first non-blank character #) ignored. A file with a match must be neutralised or reviewed at its exact SHA-256.
binary_scope: Every non-symlink file in a directory named bin or xbin (any depth: bin/hw included). A match must be reviewed by path.

payload.why: Google's postinstall (system/bin/updater-wrapper-system) runs google_desktop_firmware_updater: Google security chip firmware from system, AP (BIOS flash) and EC firmware (ap-ec-fw.zip) from vendor. An OpenBook payload must not run any postinstall step.

/system/etc/init/gscutil.rc.why: Ran gscutil perform-os-startup on every boot: stages Google security chip firmware (gsc.zip) and sends it vendor commands through /dev/tpm0, the PC's firmware TPM. Seen on the G14 and in the VM: started, denied by SELinux, exited 133.

/system/etc/init/gscutil-executor.rc.why: Defines IGscutilExecutor, started on demand; google_desktop_firmware_updater (Google's postinstall) installs security chip firmware through it.

/system/etc/init/check_tpm_clear.rc.why: Runs gscutil hwsec-ownership-id at post-fs-data: a transient TPM primary key, flushed, to name the TPM owner; writes /metadata/hwsec_metadata. Standard TPM 2.0 commands, no firmware or NV write in its code paths (strings). Exits 2 in the VM.

/system/etc/init/gscd.rc.why: IGsc daemon (user hsm). Passes TPM commands for Trusty's secure storage, udsattestation and check_tpm_clear. Kept: Trusty depends on it. Its firmware client (gscutil at boot, gscutil-executor) is neutralised.

/system/etc/init/udsattestation.rc.why: One-shot at boot (user hsm). On a TPM that is not a Google chip it skips provisioning ('Non-cr50: skipping UDS provisioning'); standard TPM 2.0 reads. Exits 1 in the VM.

/system/etc/init/timberslide.rc.why: Chrome EC log reader. Google's kernel has no Chrome EC support (CONFIG_CHROME_PLATFORMS is not set), so there is no /dev/cros_ec.

/system/etc/init/ec_crash_collector.rc.why: Chrome EC crash reader at boot completion; no Chrome EC in the kernel.

/vendor/etc/ueventd.rc.why: OpenBook's vendor: /dev/tpm* 0660 hsm hsm, Ruby's own rule, so gscd can reach the firmware TPM for Trusty.

/apex/com.android.hardware.authsecret/et.why: OpenBook's vendor APEX: AOSP's example AuthSecret HAL (keeps the secret in memory), running as user hsm. It sends no TPM commands.

reviewed_binaries./system/bin/gscutil: boot start neutralised; check_tpm_clear runs its hwsec-ownership-id subcommand
reviewed_binaries./system/bin/gsctool: Google security chip tool; no init trigger; /dev/tpm* is hsm-only
reviewed_binaries./system/bin/google_desktop_firmware_upda: only Google's postinstall runs it; OpenBook payloads have none (payload check)
reviewed_binaries./system/bin/updater-wrapper-system: Google's postinstall program; OpenBook payloads have none (payload check)
reviewed_binaries./system/bin/ectool: Chrome EC tool; no Chrome EC in the kernel
reviewed_binaries./system/bin/trunks_send: TPM command tool through gscd; no init trigger
reviewed_binaries./system_ext/bin/fwupd_splash: draws a firmware-update splash through SurfaceFlinger (bootanim_exec); no init trigger
